A federal appeals court on Friday ruled in favor of Ohio and Tennessee that they can regulate sports-related event contracts from Kalshi

The 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Cincinnati ruled that Kaslhi did not demonstrate those contracts were “swaps” that should instead face regulation from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Judge Julia Smith ​Gibbons wrote that swaps typically involve financial measures and instruments for hedging against risks, instead of for gaming-related contracts.
The decision vacates a preliminary injunction issued by a Tennessee federal judge ​and upholds the denial of an injunction against Ohio.
"The ruling shows exactly why ​a state-by-state patchwork doesn't work," Kalshi spokesperson Dani Lever told
. "Markets can't operate when the rules change at every state line, ⁠which is why Congress created a single federal regulator with nationwide rules."

Kalshi lost a similar case in August, allowing Nevada gambling laws to apply to its platform. It won a case in November that it is not subject to New Jersey gambling laws, though that state is appealing the decision to the US Supreme Court.

title: Kalshi loses appeals court ruling on state regulation of prediction markets
